The stored Cost of Sales (20,461,718,000 and 18,532,427,000) exceeded revenue, which is impossible, and exceeded it by exactly the printed gross profit, so the stored pair Revenue minus Gross Profit reproduces the bad figure: 12,492,822,000 minus 4,523,926,000 equals 7,968,896,000 and 11,388,808,000 minus 4,245,189,000 equals 7,143,619,000. The Gross profit and Gross profit Total cells carried the negative of that same amount. The printed gross profit is the figure the row already held in its Gross Profit variant, and it is confirmed by the bridge to the printed profit before tax in the same filing. Source: Crown Paints Kenya Plc audited results for the year ended 31 December 2023 (NSE filing library), whose commentary prints turnover of KShs 12.5 billion against KShs 11.4 billion and profit before tax of KShs 14 million against KShs 1.1 billion. FY2023: 4,523,926,000 plus other income 458,427,000 less administration 2,713,905,000 less selling and distribution 1,720,174,000 less finance costs 256,571,000 plus net expected credit loss reversals 277,490,000 equals 14,213,000, which is the printed KShs 14 million. FY2022: 4,245,189,000 plus 411,603,000 less 2,223,006,000 less 1,360,185,000 less 216,110,000 plus 215,379,000 equals 1,072,870,000, which is the printed KShs 1,073 million. Gross margin becomes 36.2 per cent and 37.3 per cent, in line with the 39.1 per cent and 42.4 per cent the same company prints for FY2024 and FY2025, where the negative margins previously rendered were a sign fault and not a result.
